extraFacts.fact: Gast air motor model numbers are built from a size prefix (1AM, 2AM, 4AM, 6AM, 8AM, 16AM), a type code (NCC, NCW, NRV, ARV, FCC, FCW, FRV) and a model number with an optional suffix. Gast air motors with LL or NLP in the model number can operate with or without air-line lubrication; Gast still recommends lubrication for optimal service and life. Gast offers non-lubricated versions in most sizes.
extraFacts.source: Gast Manufacturing air motor operation and maintenance manual, Part No. 45-200; Gast product page 2AM-NRV-89LL (gastmfg.com)

extraFacts.fact: Ingersoll Rand M002 Series air motors cover 0.11 to 0.25 hp, M004 Series 0.31 to 0.5 hp and M007 Series 0.64 to 0.85 hp; all are in-line planetary gear multi-vane air motors. In Ingersoll Rand's tables RVR models are listed as reversible and RHR models as non-reversible, and the three-digit group after the rotation code tracks the gear reduction: higher numbers give lower free speed and higher stall torque.
extraFacts.source: Ingersoll Rand Power Tools, M002, M004 and M007 Series Air Motors product pages (powertools.ingersollrand.com)

extraFacts.fact: Rotary vane air motor behaviour: speed is governed by the air flow admitted and torque by the supply pressure at the motor; an air motor can be stalled or overloaded without damage and can be reversed by switching the supply between ports on reversible models; output falls when pressure at the inlet drops. Exhaust air is normally silenced with a muffler. Planetary gear heads put the output shaft in line with the motor axis, spur gear heads offset it.
extraFacts.source: Gast Manufacturing Air Motors catalogue, air motor principles; Ingersoll Rand Air Motors product catalogue, gear motor overview

extraFacts.fact: HS heading 8412 covers other engines and motors; subheading 8412.31 covers linear-acting pneumatic power engines (cylinders) and 8412.39 covers other pneumatic power engines and motors, which includes rotary air motors and air gearmotors.

Air motor control valves: a one-way (non-reversible) air motor is started and stopped with a 3/2 directional valve; a reversible motor needs a 5/3 directional valve (or a pair of 3/2 valves) that sends supply to one port while the other exhausts. Valve and line size must pass the motor's air consumption.
extraFacts.source: ISO 1219-1 graphical symbols and valve designation; Gast Manufacturing Air Motors catalogue, motor controls

faqs.q: What is a Gast 2AM series air motor used for?
faqs.a: The Gast 2AM is a compact four-vane rotary air motor of up to 0.95 hp, used to drive mixers, conveyors, winders and small machines where an electric motor is unwanted. This listing holds 23 part numbers with 1/4" ports, in clockwise, counter-clockwise and reversible builds and face, foot, hub or flange mounting.

faqs.q: How do you read a Gast 2AM part number such as 2AM-NCW-7ALL?
faqs.a: In 2AM-NCW-7ALL, 2AM is the motor size, N marks 1/4" NPT ports, CW clockwise rotation and 7A the model, while the LL suffix marks a motor that can run with or without lubrication. In this range A in the type code means BSP ports (2AM-ARV-92), CC is counter-clockwise and RV reversible, as in 2AM-NRV-89LL.

faqs.q: What power and speed do Gast 2AM air motors give?
faqs.a: Standard Gast 2AM motors are rated 0.95 hp at 3,000 rpm with 7 bar maximum pressure, while the LL and NLP versions are rated 0.55 hp at 2,000 rpm with 5.6 bar maximum. Choose on the torque and speed you need at the air pressure actually available at the machine, not the compressor setting.

faqs.q: Which Gast 2AM models have 1/4" BSP rather than NPT ports?
faqs.a: The 2AM-ARV and 2AM-ACC models in this listing, such as 2AM-ARV-92, 2AM-ARV-93 and 2AM-ACC-88, have 1/4" BSP ports; the N and F type codes, such as 2AM-NRV-160 and 2AM-FCW-13LL, have 1/4" NPT. Match the fitting thread to the port so the inlet seals without forcing a mixed thread.

faqs.q: What is the maximum air pressure for a Gast 2AM air motor?
faqs.a: Gast states 81 to 102 psi (5.6 to 7 bar) maximum for the 2AM series, depending on the model: 7 bar for the standard 0.95 hp motors and 5.6 bar for the LL and NLP versions. The listing also gives a maximum air consumption of 30 CFM and a maximum sound level of 76 dBA.

faqs.q: Do Gast 2AM LL and NLP air motors need oil in the air supply?
faqs.a: No. Gast says motors with LL or NLP in the model number, such as 2AM-NRV-89LL and 2AM-NCW-7BNLP, can run with or without lubrication, though Gast still recommends oil for longest vane life. The other 2AM models expect lubricated air from a [filter-regulator-lubricator](/c/air-preparation-frl).

faqs.q: What documents can be supplied with a Gast 2AM air motor?
faqs.a: This listing carries no certificates, so ask for what your project needs when you enquire, typically the maker's certificate of conformity and a commercial invoice showing United States origin. Quote the full Gast 2AM part number so the paperwork matches the motor supplied.

faqs.q: What valves and fittings connect to a Gast 2AM air motor?
faqs.a: A Gast 2AM motor needs a 1/4" BSP or NPT supply fitting to suit its ports, a filtered and regulated air line, and a control valve: a 3/2 valve for one-way motors or a 5/3 valve to run a reversible 2AM-NRV in both directions. Valves are on our [solenoid valves shelf](/c/pneumatic-solenoid-valves) and flow controls for speed on the [flow control shelf](/c/pneumatic-flow-check-valves).

faqs.q: How do you control the speed of a Gast 2AM air motor?
faqs.a: Control a Gast 2AM's speed by throttling the air flow, usually with a flow control on the exhaust, and control its torque by setting the supply pressure with a regulator. A 2AM can stall under load without damage, which makes it suitable for tensioning and winding duties.

faqs.q: What is the difference between Gast 2AM and Gast 4AM air motors?
faqs.a: The 2AM is the smaller motor, at 0.95 hp and 3,000 rpm with 1/4" ports, while the [Gast 4AM series](/p/gast-4am-series-air-motors) gives 1.7 hp at 3,000 rpm with 1/4" or 3/8" ports. Pick the 2AM where space and air consumption matter; pick the 4AM where the load needs more torque.

faqs.q: What is the Gast 4AM series air motor?
faqs.a: The Gast 4AM is a reversible four-vane rotary air motor rated up to 1.7 hp at 3,000 rpm, used on mixers, agitators, hoists and conveyors. This listing covers 16 part numbers in standard and LL/NLP versions with 1/4" NPT, 3/8" NPT or 3/8" BSPP ports and a keyed output shaft.

faqs.q: What do the codes ARV, FRV and NRV mean in Gast 4AM part numbers?
faqs.a: All three mark reversible Gast 4AM motors: ARV models such as 4AM-ARV-119LL have 3/8" BSPP ports, NRV models such as 4AM-NRV-130A have NPT ports, and FRV models such as 4AM-FRV-13A are listed with 1/4" NPT. A trailing LL or NLP marks a motor that can run with or without lubrication.

faqs.q: What power ratings are available in the Gast 4AM air motor range?
faqs.a: Gast 4AM motors in this listing come at two ratings: 1.7 hp at 3,000 rpm with 7 bar maximum for standard models such as 4AM-NRV-54, and 1.05 hp at 2,000 rpm with 5.6 bar maximum for LL and NLP models such as 4AM-NRV-70CLL. Most rows show 56 lb-in torque.

faqs.q: Which Gast 4AM motors have 3/8" ports instead of 1/4"?
faqs.a: The 4AM-NRV-130 family (130A, 130LL, 130NLP) has 3/8" NPT ports and the 4AM-ARV-119LL and 119NLP have 3/8" BSPP; the rest of this listing, such as 4AM-NRV-22A and 4AM-FRV-13A, has 1/4" NPT. The larger port suits longer supply runs where pressure drop would cut torque.

faqs.q: What air pressure is a Gast 4AM air motor rated for?
faqs.a: Gast states 80 to 102 psi (5.5 to 7 bar) maximum for the 4AM, by model: 7 bar for the 1.7 hp standard motors and 5.6 bar for most LL and NLP versions, with 4AM-NRV-54ALL listed at 5.5 bar. The listing gives 87 dBA as the maximum sound level.

faqs.q: Can a Gast 4AM air motor run without a lubricator?
faqs.a: Only the LL and NLP versions, such as 4AM-NRV-22BNLP and 4AM-NRV-54ALL, are made to run with or without oil; Gast still recommends lubrication for best life. Standard 4AM models need lubricated air, so fit a lubricator, explained in our [FRL guide](/blog/frl-filter-regulator-lubricator-guide).

faqs.q: Which certificates come with a Gast 4AM air motor?
faqs.a: No certificates are held on this listing, so state your requirement when ordering: usually a maker certificate of conformity and proof of United States origin for customs. Give the exact Gast 4AM part number, including any LL or NLP suffix, so the documents match the motor.

faqs.q: What is needed to install and control a Gast 4AM reversible air motor?
faqs.a: A Gast 4AM needs clean, regulated air at its 1/4" or 3/8" port, a 5/3 or 4-way valve to switch the supply between ports for reversing, and an exhaust muffler. Valves are on our [solenoid valves and manifolds shelf](/c/pneumatic-solenoid-valves); regulators and filters are on the FRL shelf.

faqs.q: How do you maintain a Gast 4AM rotary vane air motor?
faqs.a: Keep the Gast 4AM supplied with filtered, dry air, keep the lubricator topped up on standard models, and replace vanes when power falls off at normal pressure. Water and dirt in the line are the usual causes of vane wear; our [air quality guide](/blog/compressed-air-quality-iso-8573-1) covers drying and filtration.

faqs.a: Both are the same 4AM motor family; this listing carries the LL/NLP and BSPP versions, while the [Gast 4AM rotary vane listing](/p/gast-4am-series-rotary-vane-air-motors) carries further standard part numbers and geared models with gear-head suffixes. Search both by part number, or send it to us.

faqs.q: What is a Gast 4AM rotary vane air motor?
faqs.a: The Gast 4AM rotary vane air motor is a reversible cast iron, four-vane motor giving 1.7 hp at 3,000 rpm and 72 cfm, with a steel keyed shaft and a muffler included. This listing holds 14 part numbers in face, foot and flange mounting, plus geared versions for low-speed, high-torque drives.

faqs.q: What do the suffixes CB20, CB60 and GR20 mean on Gast 4AM motors?
faqs.a: They mark 4AM motors supplied with a gear head: 4AM-70C-CB20 is listed at 1.1 hp with 480 in-lb torque, 4AM-70C-CB60 at 0.85 hp, and 4AM-RV-75-GR20 at 640 lb-in. Plain models such as 4AM-NRV-130 run direct at 3,000 rpm; choose a geared one when the load needs low speed.

faqs.q: Which mounting styles does the Gast 4AM rotary vane motor come in?
faqs.a: This 4AM listing includes face mount (4AM-ARV-119, 4AM-NRV-130), foot mount (4AM-FRV-63A), flange mount (4AM-RV-75) and the flanged 4AM-NRV-50C with a 5/8" shaft. Gast allows mounting at any angle, so pick the style that suits the machine frame.

faqs.q: What port sizes do Gast 4AM rotary vane air motors have?
faqs.a: The Gast 4AM rotary vane motors here have female inlets of 1/4" NPT (4AM-FRV-63A, 4AM-RV-75), 3/8" NPT (4AM-NRV-130) or 3/8" BSP (4AM-ARV-119 and 4AM-ARV-120). Use the full port size up to the motor so the 72 cfm demand does not starve the vanes.

faqs.q: What are the torque and temperature ratings of the Gast 4AM rotary vane motor?
faqs.a: Gast rates the standard 4AM at 1.7 hp, 3,000 rpm and 35 in-lb torque, with 56 lb-in in the size table, for ambient temperatures from 34°F to 248°F. Maximum pressure is 7 bar on most models; the lubricated 4AM-NRV-22F and 4AM-NRV-70C are listed at 100 psi.

faqs.q: What is the Gast 4AM rotary vane air motor made of?
faqs.a: The Gast 4AM rotary vane motor has a painted cast iron housing and a steel output shaft with a #3 Woodruff key. Cast iron suits plant-floor duty; keep condensate out of the supply, as standing water in the body is what attacks vanes and bore.

faqs.q: Does the Gast 4AM rotary vane air motor come with a test certificate?
faqs.a: No certificate is held for this listing, so ask for a maker certificate of conformity or origin documents with the enquiry if your project needs them. Quote the complete Gast 4AM part number, such as 4AM-NRV-22B, so the paperwork matches the unit.

faqs.q: What exhaust and supply parts go with a Gast 4AM rotary vane motor?
faqs.a: The Gast 4AM rotary vane motor ships with a muffler; you add a supply fitting for the 1/4" or 3/8" port, a regulator and filter, and a valve to start, stop or reverse it. Spare mufflers and fittings are on our [fittings and silencers shelf](/c/pneumatic-fittings-silencers).

faqs.q: How should a Gast 4AM rotary vane motor be sized for a load?
faqs.a: Size a Gast 4AM on the torque and speed needed at the pressure available at the motor, since output falls as inlet pressure drops. Our [air motor sizing guide](/blog/air-motors-guide) explains the torque curve; where the load needs high torque at low speed, a geared model such as 4AM-RV-75-GR20 fits better.

faqs.q: Is the Gast 4AM-NRV-22B the same motor as the 4AM-NRV-22BNLP?
faqs.a: They share the 4AM-NRV-22 base but differ in rating: 4AM-NRV-22B here is a standard motor at 1.7 hp and 7 bar, while 4AM-NRV-22BNLP on the [Gast 4AM listing](/p/gast-4am-series-air-motors) is rated 1.05 hp at 5.6 bar and can run with or without lubrication. Order by full part number.

faqs.q: What is a Gast 6AM series air motor used for?
faqs.a: The Gast 6AM is a reversible rotary vane air motor rated 4 hp at 3,000 rpm, used for heavier drives such as mixers, pumps, winches and conveyors. This listing has four part numbers, 6AM-ARV-54, 6AM-ARV-55, 6AM-FRV-71 and 6AM-NRV-7B, all with 1/2" ports and a keyed shaft.

faqs.q: What is the difference between Gast 6AM-ARV-54 and 6AM-NRV-7B?
faqs.a: Both are 4 hp, 3,000 rpm reversible Gast 6AM motors; the ARV models (6AM-ARV-54 and 6AM-ARV-55) have 1/2" BSPP ports, while 6AM-NRV-7B and 6AM-FRV-71 have 1/2" NPT. Pick the thread to match your fittings, then the mounting to suit the machine.

faqs.q: How much air does a Gast 6AM air motor consume?
faqs.a: The Gast 6AM is listed at up to 128 CFM maximum air consumption, so the supply line, valve and FRL must pass that flow at the working pressure. An undersized 1/2" line or valve starves the motor and cuts its 4 hp output.

faqs.q: What torque does a Gast 6AM air motor deliver?
faqs.a: Our size table lists 115 lb-in torque for each Gast 6AM model, with 4 hp at 3,000 rpm and 7 bar maximum pressure. If the load needs more torque at lower speed, consider a geared motor or the larger [Gast 8AM series](/p/gast-8am-series-air-motors).

faqs.q: What is the maximum pressure and noise level of a Gast 6AM air motor?
faqs.a: Each Gast 6AM in this listing is rated for 7 bar maximum pressure, and the listing gives a maximum sound level of 90 dBA. Fit an exhaust muffler, and hearing protection may still be needed near a motor running at full load.

faqs.q: Does a Gast 6AM air motor need lubricated air?
faqs.a: Yes. The four Gast 6AM models here carry no LL or NLP suffix, so plan to run them on oil mist from a line lubricator, as Gast reserves lube-optional running for LL and NLP models. Set it up as described in our [FRL guide](/blog/frl-filter-regulator-lubricator-guide), with a filter ahead of it.

faqs.q: What certification is available for a Gast 6AM air motor?
faqs.a: This listing holds no certificates, so state what you need, such as a maker certificate of conformity and United States origin papers, when you request a quote. Quote the full Gast 6AM part number so the documents match.

faqs.q: Which valve is needed to reverse a Gast 6AM air motor?
faqs.a: To run a Gast 6AM in both directions, use a valve that switches air between its two 1/2" ports while exhausting the other, typically a 5/3 closed- or exhaust-centre valve sized for 128 CFM. Valves are on our [manual and pilot air valves shelf](/c/pneumatic-control-valves).

faqs.q: How do you set the speed and torque of a Gast 6AM air motor?
faqs.a: Set the Gast 6AM's speed by restricting air flow, ideally on the exhaust, and its torque with the supply regulator. The motor can stall under overload without damage and restarts when the load eases, which suits winches and tensioning drives.

faqs.q: Should I choose a Gast 4AM or a Gast 6AM air motor?
faqs.a: Choose the Gast 6AM when the load needs 4 hp and 115 lb-in; the [Gast 4AM](/p/gast-4am-series-air-motors) gives 1.7 hp and 56 lb-in from a smaller 1/4" or 3/8" port. The 6AM's higher air demand of up to 128 CFM needs a bigger supply.

faqs.q: What is the Gast 8AM series air motor?
faqs.a: The Gast 8AM is a 5 hp reversible rotary vane air motor running at 2,500 rpm with 7 bar maximum pressure, for heavier drives than the 6AM. This listing holds three part numbers: 8AM-ARV-70, 8AM-ARV-71 and 8AM-NRV-42A, all with 1/2" ports.

faqs.q: What is the difference between Gast 8AM-ARV-70 and 8AM-ARV-71?

faqs.q: Which Gast 8AM model suits an NPT air supply?
faqs.a: Gast 8AM-NRV-42A is the NPT model in this listing, with 1/2" NPT ports, face mounting, a 3/4" shaft and an M30-KEYSQ key; the two ARV models have BSP ports and an IEC flange. Match both the thread and the shaft before swapping one for another.

faqs.q: How much compressed air does a Gast 8AM air motor need?
faqs.a: The Gast 8AM is listed at up to 175 CFM maximum air consumption at 7 bar, so the compressor, line, valve and FRL must all pass that flow. Starving the 1/2" port is the commonest reason an 8AM falls short of its 5 hp.

faqs.q: What torque and noise ratings apply to the Gast 8AM air motor?
faqs.a: Our size table lists 185 lb-in torque for every Gast 8AM model at 5 hp and 2,500 rpm, and the listing gives a maximum sound level of 105 dBA. Pipe the exhaust away or fit a large muffler on an 8AM in a staffed area.

faqs.q: Does the Gast 8AM air motor need a lubricator?

faqs.q: Will a Gast 8AM-ARV motor fit an IEC flange gearbox?

faqs.q: How should a Gast 8AM air motor be controlled?
faqs.a: Control the Gast 8AM's speed by throttling air flow and its torque with the supply regulator, and reverse it with a valve that swaps supply and exhaust between its ports. Our [air motor guide](/blog/air-motors-guide) explains how torque falls with pressure and how to size at your supply.

faqs.q: How does the Gast 8AM compare with the Gast 6AM air motor?
